Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $35 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members. Brightline would separately pay up to $3.5 million in court-approved fees and expenses; any amount not awarded would go to the class. We are open to discussing the fund amount, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic distribution is appropriate given the available records. To resolve the case promptly while accounting for the remaining certification and merits risks, Brightline proposes a $30 million class fund plus up to $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus up to $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing agreement and any unawarded fees going to the class. We will submit the settlement for court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial automatic-distribution fund. The class can be identified and paid without claims, so a claims-made structure would needlessly reduce recovery. Keep fees separate and ensure any amount the court does not award goes to the class rather than Brightline.

The opening proposal is within the $40 million authorization and has court-friendly distribution and fee terms, but there is room to reduce total cash outlay. Counter with automatic payments and no fee reversion while lowering the fund and fees.

The $30 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted merits-only expected trial recovery, before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The separate fee provision does not affect firm compensation; there is no clear sailing or fee reversion. Acceptance serves the class well.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the proposed settlement through arm’s-length negotiations. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed in the same negotiations; counsel did not defer fee discussions until after agreeing on class relief. The settlement provides a $30 million class fund distributed automatically to identified members, plus up to $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses. There is no clear-sailing agreement, and any fees not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. In counsel’s judgment, the certain, automatic recovery is fair in light of the remaining certification risk, the risk of no recovery at trial, and the expected delay of litigation.
